posts.name: Kaivax
posts.cooked:
Now that players around the world are leveling up in WoW: Forever, we’ve identified a few class issues that we feel need some immediate changes. Today, we’re still investigating these issues and working through them with a plan to release hotfixes on Tuesday, November 10 to address:

  • We’ve seen that Hunter pets and Warlock Voidwalkers are not as durable as tanks as we would like them to be. Our intent is for their effectiveness to be relatively the same as in Classic Era. We will adjust their stats as necessary to accomplish this.
  • Affliction Warlock reports indicate that always channeling Wrack is superior to also casting damage-over-time abilities like Siphon Life, Corruption, and Bane of Agony. We will make adjustments to make sure those are always worthwhile to cast combined with Wrack, without affecting Affliction Warlocks’ total damage output.
  • Enhancement Shamans are finding that Intellect and Spellpower are superior stats compared to Strength and Attack Power. We plan to make changes so that Strength is always their strongest stat, and Enhancement Shamans will not prefer gear intended for Mages and Warlocks. Ideally, Enhancement’s best items have Strength or Attack Power, along with some Intellect and/or Spell Power.

Please note: Enhancement Shaman players who are leveling up will want to collect Strength and Attack Power gear from now on.

We may find new issues over the weekend, and we will keep you updated. Our plan is to make class balance changes on Tuesday, and then on future Tuesdays if necessary. Thank you very much for your feedback!

posts.name: SCE
posts.cooked:
Boomy is actually so absurdly unplayable.

The devs said sooo many times that they wanted druid’s wrath to basically be the druid’s wanding.

But not only do wands deal more damage until you get loads of SP, you need to invest 8 talents into resto to get 70% spellpushback + manareg, and 8 talent points into boomy (5x wrath 3x moonglow), and all of that only for it to STILL get crushed by spellpushback when attacked, it destroys the 5s mana rule, takes ages to come semi-online, and once you actually get deeper into the balance tree, it literally is ONLY a star fire buff-tool, and nothing else.

Boomys are literally worse classic combat rogues that now have a builder and spender + the fact that star fire, even with the talents, but especially before, soaks up an ABSURD amount of mana from us, to deal actually quite disappointing damage for such an absurd cast time + the even more absurd amount of talent points we have to invest just to make it SEMI useable.

Like 50% of Boomy talents could get removed and just baked into the spec and nothing of value would be lost.

The star fire cast-time reduction should be part of the R1 5/5 wrath node, moonglow should be gone and baked in, the entangling roots talents should be combined, Nature’s Splendor should connect directly to Genesis, which also shouldn’t be a 5-point talent that is exclusively a resto talent anyways.

Moonkin Form is a joke when the only thing you really get from it is an increased CC proc chance, which is either useless, as you shouldn’t rely on JUST twice the proccs from it, or so absurdly mandatory that you cannot play the class without it, especially given that the benefits it provides (in PvE) are getting worse with faster kill times, especially when the aura it provides is provided by both cats AND bears a whole 10 levels earlier, which are also the better specs to bring instead of us for it.

Like 90% of the boomy tree skill points are either talent points for the other specs, or stuff that progressively makes boomy only LESS painful to play, as if boomy is literally starting off behind by an absurd amount, and needs the talents JUST to catch up to the actual baseline ( insane manacosts and cast-time especially).

A spec should feel cool as a baseline, and then just get BETTER, but boomy is so terrible that especially early, wand-casters crush boomy dps while having full regen, while we OOM, get pushed back, and just have a miserable experience.

Just the fact alone that the BEST talents for boomy until mid-game+ are literally going 13 points deep into resto, because the spell-pushback + 10% OVERALL damage + 50% manareg while casting are worlds better than especially 10% DOT damage.

Talking about DoT damage, why TF is the Dot/HoT talent in the boomy tree, while less than 30% of our damage is from DoTs, while the 10% overall damage talent is in the resto tree?
Similar to the manareg while-casting talent, which would be worlds better in the boomy tree as they ARE constantly casting, while restos are putting Hots up and then waiting for their 5s rule to kick in while their Hots tick?

Or why are there 3 talents (worth 9 skill points) of mana-cost-related talents in our tree?
Why do we need 14+ talent points just to make Starfire playable? (and then randomly too much?)
Why was Wrath literally just made into a Starfire buffer?
Why is Starfire by far more than half our damage?
Why is Wrath absolutely terrible until it gets saved/replaced by Starfire?
Why is there not a single talent for Hurricane?
Why isn’t there a single talent for Swarm?
Why isn’t there a single talent for Thorns?
Why are we the only spec that needs 4 1 SKILLPOINTS in our tree?!
Why is our Capstone just worse than the Feral equivalent, and could possibly end up giving us 0 benefit once fights get short enough that OOC proccs become irrelevant, especially when there will be another Feral to provide the aura anyways, instead of even a simple 15% spell damage, or whatever buff?

A really good example of a more healthy damage distribution would be the Cata Boomy, if we obviously exclude the spells that aren’t in Classic, so Wrath, Starfire, Moonfire, and Swarm.

Cata Boomy P1=

Wrath>>Starfire>Swarm=Moonfire

The most important rule when it comes to any rotation, is that the “builder/filler” should almost never be below the “spender”, because that makes anything besides the “spender” feel like wasted time, instead of a cool bonus.
And currently, you just want to get through those 2 mandatory Wrath casts out of the way ASAP to get back to your only big damage dealing ability, which is Starfire.

Currently, the rough 2m damage breakdown at 60 is:

Starfire 54%~
Wrath 15%~
Swarm 15%~
Moonfire 15%~

This perfectly reflects the problem, even if you were to reduce the overall mana costs of all our spells, or just aura-buff Boomy by 30%, the issue would still be the same.

Following the intended/enforced Boomy rotation, one single spell, that we also only get to properly use VERY MUCH later in the game with talents & gear, deals far more damage than the combined rest of our spells, and specifically the spell that we are pressing the most, especially while leveling, Wrath.

During Beta, at least in Dungeons, Boomys were welcome because their scaling Thorns buff was significantly more helpful than the one from Ferals or even Restos, but after absolutely nuking even the one thing that made them a welcome sight even in dungeons, we are left with all of the problems, and non of the benefits.

And the solution to that problem is the solution to the biggest problem of Boomy, and something absolutely no one was asking for.

Stop trying to make Wrath an overall worse wand filler, (yes that also includes making it cost 0 mana like you mentioned in the podcast + 100% pushback reduction or other stuff), and just make it the bigger part of the bread & butter mix between Wrath & Starfire, get rid of the absurdly low damage & high manacost (that you try to balance with absurdly high & mandatory manacost reduction talents), maybe make Eclipse work both ways so that empowered Starfire casts also buff the damage of Wrath, so that Starfire doesn’t soak up 9 talent points just to not take ages to cast, while Wrath regains its power and isn’t worse than pure Bear AAs while low level.

At it’s core, the rotation should respect and be guided by easy rules:

  1. Both DoTs should be very rewarding to keep up, while not overtaking hardcasts on ST, and not feel like they are just mathematically simmed to be optimal for the global they take to cast.
  2. Starfire should feel like a less frequent, long, but rewarding cast, not just at lvl 40+.
  3. Wrath should feel and perform like the primary driver in ST (like melee’s AAs, Hunter’s autoshot, etc like especially Feral already perfectly delivers with their AA + Shred dmg mix compared to Rip/Bite/Rake)

If you had followed these simple guidelines, you wouldn’t have had the Wrath problem during beta, or the current Wrath problem even AFTER a 50% base-buff, which should’ve been a VERY clear sign, not to mention all the SIMS that were available since early Beta & now.

There is a reason that absolutely no one plays Balance right now while leveling, and it isn’t just because Feral is running faster, it is because they feel handicapped, without absolutely any unique benefit, not even being able to off-heal.

I’m just glad for my fellow Ferals, that they didn’t receive the Retail Feral treatment, and that their lvl 60 breakdown isn’t 50%+ Ferocious Bite, while the other damage sources are far below that. (even if they have their very own unique problems with how horrible shifting power is, especially after seeing the amazing Rogue changes)

posts.name: DoomGuy
posts.cooked:
Please don’t kill Spell-int build.

I think Enhancement should have at least two, or even three, competitive builds instead of forcing everyone into the same stat priority and playstyle.

One player might enjoy Spellhance, focusing on Spell Power, Intellect, elemental damage and spells. Another might prefer a traditional Strength-based build focused on Stormstrike, weapon damage and auto-attacks. There could even be other interesting variations.

Not every build needs to have exactly the same DPS, and not every player needs to follow the same gearing strategy. The most important thing is that different playstyles remain viable and enjoyable.

I really hope Blizzard moves away from the idea that every spec must have one clearly defined stat priority, where one stat is always first, another is second, and everyone is expected to copy the same build.

One of the best things about an MMORPG is experimenting, theorycrafting and discovering unusual combinations that work. Let players create their own builds instead of pushing everyone toward the same template.

Please don’t take away a playstyle that people genuinely enjoy. Keep Spellhance alive and give players the freedom to choose how they want to play Enhancement.

posts.name: Loimulohi
posts.cooked:
I’m quite interested in seeing what this will look like for Shamans. I’m leveling as a Shaman tank and gearing mostly “traditionally”, favouring Agility, Strength, and Attack Power over Intellect and Spell Power. I’m also talenting into defensive Enhancement, taking Guardian Totems, dodge, and eventually stamina (just got to level 25).

And I have to say: it’s not exactly all roses: I mostly play with little or no mana, my mana regeneration is poor when not casting from having no spirit to speak of, the 150% AP from Intellect is worth 120 AP so about 9 DPS, and compared to Protection Warriors I’ve been in dungeons with my threat generation is a fair bit worse. At least my auto attack hits pretty hard and crits often, though.

Had I geared into Intellect more I may have at least had mana and mana regeneration, which would’ve probably meant I also have better threat generation. Talenting into Restoration might’ve also been better since I’d have gotten hit, mana regeneration, a bit of health, and Water Shield.

I personally quite prefer the club&board style/fantasy of Shaman tanking, and the 2h “swing big club fast” fantasy of Enhancement DPS. Of course spells, especially shocks, are there but I don’t particularly view them as the main thing. Hence I’ve felt the focus on Intellect as vaguely offending. I’d have assumed the opposite to be done: eg. increased mana from Strength or Agility, increased Spell Power from Strength, Agility, or Attack Power. But of course that makes for a fairly “cookie-cutter” sort of build strategy. On the other hand, trying to balance Strength, Agility, Intellect, Spirit, and Stamina all at the same time on a single class / talent tree focus is going to be impossible: one stat will outshine others, and it’ll be hard to keep the others competitive without making the total whole an overpowered mess.

Blizzard have their work cut out for them: here’s to hoping they’ll find good solutions (and don’t leave too much of the changes up for Claude to implement).
